title: Phase 2: Tantivy Indexing & Search
description:
## Phase 2: Tantivy Indexing & Search

### Objectives
- Build Tantivy index from normalized sessions (BM25 scoring, faceted fields)
- Implement incremental indexing on scrape (no full rebuild required)
- Build three-tier tag extraction pipeline (explicit, structural, keyword list)
- Implement fuzzy search via Tantivy's Levenshtein term queries
- Implement "more like this" search via Tantivy's MoreLikeThisQuery
- Build context budget packing with greedy knapsack algorithm
- Implement structured JSON output mode for agent consumption

### CLI Commands
- `agentscribe index rebuild|stats|optimize` — manage the Tantivy search index
- `agentscribe search` — query interface (primary interface for agents)
- `agentscribe status` — show tracked agents, session counts, daemon state

### Tantivy Index Schema
See plan.md lines 347-391 for the full schema definition. Key fields:
- Full-text: `content`, `summary`, `solution_summary`, `code_content`
- Faceted: `session_id`, `source_agent`, `project`, `tags`, `outcome`, `error_fingerprint`, `file_paths`, `git_commits`, `doc_type`
- Code artifacts: `code_language`, `code_file_path`, `code_is_final`
- Date/numeric: `timestamp`, `turn_count`

### Tag Extraction Pipeline (Three-Tier)
1. **Explicit:** tool names from `tool_call` events (`Edit`, `Bash`, `Read`), languages from code fence markers (`` ```rust `` → `rust`)
2. **Structural:** file extensions from `file_paths` (`.rs` → `rust`, `.py` → `python`), command names from Bash content (`docker`, `git`, `npm`, `cargo`, `kubectl`), error types from `error_fingerprints`
3. **Keyword list:** match content against bundled technology dictionary (~200 terms: frameworks, databases, cloud services, protocols). Exact word-boundary matches only.

### Search Features
- Full-text BM25 search across session content and summaries (default mode)
- Error lookup: `--error <pattern>` against normalized error fingerprints
- Code search: `--code <query> [--lang <lang>]` for code artifacts
- Solution-only: `--solution-only` to return only extracted solutions
- Similar sessions: `--like <session-id>` using Tantivy MoreLikeThis
- Filters: `--agent`, `--project`, `--since`/`--before`, `--tag`, `--outcome`, `--type`, `--model`
- Output: `--max-results`, `--snippet-length`, `--token-budget <n>` (greedy knapsack)
- Structured: `--json` for agent consumption

### Content Truncation Policy
- `user` and `assistant` content: indexed in full
- `tool_call` content: indexed in full
- `tool_result` content: truncated to first 1000 chars per event
- Total document content capped at 500KB (trim middle if exceeded: keep first 250KB + last 250KB)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tantivy index creation with full schema (all fields from plan.md)
- [ ] One document per session, concatenated with role prefixes
- [ ] Content truncation policy implemented (1000 chars for tool_result, 500KB total cap)

- [ ] `agentscribe index optimize` compacts segments

title: Context budget packing (token-budget knapsack)
description:
Implement --token-budget <n> greedy knapsack algorithm for optimal context packing.

## Scope
- Token estimation: ceil(chars / 4)
- Greedy knapsack: rank by relevance, pack until budget full
- Adaptive: choose between fewer results with longer snippets vs more results with shorter snippets
- Replaces --max-results + --snippet-length when specified

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] --token-budget flag accepted
- [ ] Results fit within specified token budget
- [ ] Maximizes total relevance coverage within budget
- [ ] Works with --solution-only (shorter results = more fit)
- [ ] JSON output includes token counts per result

title: Search-on-error shell hook
description:
Shell integration that auto-queries AgentScribe when commands fail.

## Scope
- `agentscribe shell-hook bash|zsh|fish` generates shell snippet
- Uses PROMPT_COMMAND (bash) / precmd (zsh) to detect non-zero exit

- Background subprocess (&), never blocks the shell
- Result in temp file, printed on next prompt if available
- No stderr capture (fragile, breaks pipes)

## Setup
- `eval "$(agentscribe shell-hook bash)"` in .bashrc
- `eval "$(agentscribe shell-hook zsh)"` in .zshrc

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Generates correct shell snippets for bash, zsh, fish
- [ ] Background search never blocks shell prompt
- [ ] One-line hint displayed when previous error has a known solution
- [ ] Discards result silently if search takes longer than one prompt cycle

title: context subcommand — pre-task priming query for agent workers
description:
Implement `agentscribe context "<task description>"` — a purpose-built pre-task query that returns a formatted, token-budget-packed context block ready for injection into an agent prompt.

## Motivation
`agentscribe search` is designed for humans typing keywords. Workers (NEEDLE, Claude Code, etc.) need a single call that returns a structured, injection-ready block combining past solutions + project conventions + file gotchas. This subcommand is that call.

## Interface
```
agentscribe context "<task description>" [--token-budget <n>] [--project <path>] [--json]
```
- `--token-budget`: default 3000. Applied globally across all three sections.
- `--project`: scope rules extraction to this path. Defaults to cwd.
- `--json`: wrap sections in a JSON object `{past_solutions, conventions, file_notes}` for programmatic assembly.

## Behavior
1. **Past solutions**: `execute_search(query=task_desc, solution_only=true, outcome=success, token_budget=budget*0.6)`
2. **Conventions**: inline rules extraction for `--project` (same pipeline as `agentscribe rules` but stdout not file)
3. **File notes**: parse task description for file path tokens, call `get_file_knowledge` for each, prepend gotchas

## Output format (default)
```
## Prior Context

### Past Solutions
[packed results]

### Project Conventions
[rules]

### File Notes
[per-file gotchas]
```

## Token budget semantics
Priority: past solutions > conventions > file notes. If budget exhausted, later sections omitted.

## NEEDLE integration point
In `NEEDLE/src/prompt/mod.rs`, `build_with_vars` context_parts assembly:
```rust
if let Ok(out) = std::process::Command::new("agentscribe")
    .args(["context", &bead.title, "--token-budget", "2000"])
    .output()
{
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);
    if !text.trim().is_empty() {
        context_parts.push(format!("## Prior Context\n{}", text.trim()));
    }
}
```

## Implementation
- New `Commands::Context` variant in `src/cli.rs`
- New `context_pack` function in `src/search.rs` assembling the three sections
- Rules extraction needs a non-file output path (refactor `rules.rs` to return `String` instead of writing file)
- ~150 lines of new code, no new dependencies

## Tests
- `tests/context_tests.rs`: empty index returns empty output, non-empty index returns formatted block, token budget truncates correctly, `--json` output is valid JSON

title: render subcommand — individual session HTML/Markdown export
description:
Implement `agentscribe render <session-id>` — renders a single archived session as a self-contained HTML file or structured Markdown for sharing and linking from commit messages.

## Motivation
Simon Willison publishes AI session transcripts as first-class versioned artifacts. AgentScribe has all the session data; it needs a render path to make individual sessions portable and shareable. The primary use case: `agentscribe render <id> --output /tmp/s.html && gh gist create /tmp/s.html` produces a permanent URL for a commit message.

## Interface
```
agentscribe render <session-id> [--output <path>] [--format html|markdown]
```
- `--output`: defaults to stdout
- `--format html`: self-contained HTML, inline CSS + JS, no CDN (default)
- `--format markdown`: alternating **User** / **Assistant** blocks with YAML frontmatter

## HTML output structure
```
<header>: project | agent | outcome | duration | models used | files touched
<conversation>: role badge + timestamp per turn; code blocks syntax-highlighted
<footer>: session ID | scraped at | "Generated by AgentScribe"
```

## CSS constraints
- Self-contained, inline, ~3KB budget
- Dark/light via `prefers-color-scheme`
- No external fonts — monospace stack only
- Code blocks: monospace, no external syntax CSS

## Syntax highlighting
- highlight.js subset: Rust, Python, TypeScript, Bash, YAML, TOML, JSON
- Embedded as `static str` constant (~50KB inlined JS)
- Full highlight.js is 500KB; subset sufficient for typical session content

## Markdown output
YAML frontmatter with metadata, then alternating fenced sections per turn. Code blocks fenced with language tags from original fence markers.

## Implementation
- New `Commands::Render` variant in `src/cli.rs`
- New `src/render.rs` with `render_html(session: &[Event], meta: &SessionMeta) -> String` and `render_markdown(...) -> String`
- highlight.js subset embedded as `const HLJS: &str = include_str!("../assets/hljs-subset.min.js")`

THE OPEN GAP: input history does NOT flow through the SCRAPE PATH. The FormatParser trait (src/parser/mod.rs around line 163) signature is fn parse(&self, source_path, plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>> with NO input-history parameter. MarkdownParser::parse (markdown.rs around line 234) calls Self::parse_content WITHOUT input history. So the scrape path never enriches timestamps today.

TASK: Decide WIRE vs DELETE and record the reasoning. Decision criterion from the parent: if it fits WITHOUT restructuring the FormatParser trait or adding scrape-path complexity, WIRE; otherwise DELETE.
- Investigate whether MarkdownParser::parse can auto-discover a sibling .aider.input.history file next to source_path and call parse_content_with_input_history WITHOUT changing the trait signature. If yes (expected), decision is WIRE.

Reasoning — auto-discovery of the sibling .aider.input.history requires NO change to the FormatParser trait and NO threading of companion data through the scrape pipeline:

1. TRAIT SIGNATURE (cited as required): src/parser/mod.rs:225 defines FormatParser::parse as fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>. It already receives source_path, which is sufficient to derive the companion path locally inside the parser. No input-history parameter needs to be added to the trait.

2. INTEGRATION POINT (named as required): auto-discover the sibling INSIDE MarkdownParser::parse. Compute source_path.parent().join(".aider.input.history"), load it best-effort, and call parse_content_with_input_history(..., Some(history)). No companion data is threaded through the scrape pipeline.

3. Graceful degradation: a missing/unreadable/empty companion returns None and parse() falls back to parse_content — no enrichment, no error, no added scrape-path complexity.

5. EDGE CASES: each plugin has at least one malformed-input fixture (truncated line / bad JSON / empty session) and the scrape skips-and-logs without failing (skip-and-log policy, plan.md Phase 1).

A plugin missing fixtures = test FAILURE (forcing-function for future plugins). {

The reflection tool (future) will call:
  agentscribe annotate <session_id> --tag <tag> --note '...'

This creates a feedback loop:

title: Reflection export API: structured behavioral data for reflection tooling
description:
The reflection tooling that will auto-tune CLAUDE.md needs a clean, structured way to consume AgentScribe data — not just full-text search results. This bead adds a reflection-oriented export command and MCP tools.

## New CLI command: agentscribe reflect

### agentscribe reflect sessions [options]
Exports a structured JSON array of sessions with behavioral metadata suitable for reflection analysis.

Output per session:
{
  session_id: string,
  agent: string,
  project: string | null,
  started: ISO8601,
  ended: ISO8601 | null,
  duration_secs: int,
  outcome: 'success' | 'failure' | 'abandoned' | 'unknown',
  summary: string | null,
  tags: string[],
  model: string | null,
  tool_call_counts: {bash: int, read: int, edit: int, write: int, ...},
  re_read_count: int,
  bash_failure_count: int,
  read_config_files: string[],
  modified_config_files: string[],
  error_fingerprints: string[],
  anti_patterns: [{pattern: string}],
  files_touched: string[],
  config_changes_after: [{file: string, minutes_after: int}]
}

### Flags
--since <duration>      (e.g. 7d, 30d, 1y)
--project <path>        Filter by project
--outcome <success|failure|abandoned>
--modified-config       Only sessions where agent modified config files
--read-config           Only sessions where agent read config files  
--json                  Output JSON (default)
--csv                   Output CSV for spreadsheet analysis
--limit <n>             Max sessions (default 1000)

### agentscribe reflect patterns [options]
Cross-session behavioral pattern summary:
- Most common tool sequences preceding failures
- Files most frequently re-read before success
- Config files most frequently modified and what outcomes precede them
- Recurring error fingerprints and their resolution rates

## New MCP tools (add to src/mcp.rs)

### agentscribe_reflect_sessions
Same as CLI but MCP-shaped. Returns behavioral session list.
Input: {since_days: int, project: string?, outcome_filter: string?, modified_config_only: bool}

### agentscribe_behavioral_signals
Given a session_id, return full behavioral signals for that session.
Input: {session_id: string}
Output: full BehavioralSignals struct as JSON

## Implementation
- New src/reflect.rs module
- New Commands::Reflect variant in src/cli.rs with Reflect::Sessions and Reflect::Patterns subcommands
- Reads behavioral_signals.json sidecars (from bf-5t70) + search index
- Falls back gracefully when sidecars not yet built (runs enrichment on-demand)

## Acceptance Criteria
- agentscribe reflect sessions --since 7d --json outputs valid structured JSON
- agentscribe reflect sessions --modified-config filters correctly
- Two new MCP tools exposed and documented
- Output schema documented in docs/cli-reference.md as stable contract

title: Config/memory file change detection: track when CLAUDE.md and similar files are modified
description:
The core signal for reflection tooling is: 'which agent behaviors preceded a config file change?' AgentScribe needs to detect when CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, memory files, or other agent config files are created/modified during or after a session.

## Problem
Git correlation (src/enrichment/git.rs) exists but:
1. Only looks at commits, not uncommitted edits
2. Does not specifically flag config/memory files vs code files
3. Does not correlate 'session happened, then config was changed within N hours'

## Two detection mechanisms needed

### 1. In-session detection (from tool_params - depends on bf-2a8w)
If a session's ToolCall events show Write/Edit calls to paths matching config file patterns, record these as 'config_writes' in BehavioralSignals (bf-5t70).
Patterns: **/CLAUDE.md, **/AGENTS.md, **/.claude/CLAUDE.md, **/memory/*.md, **/docs/notes/*.md, **/.needle/**, **/MEMORY.md

### 2. Post-session correlation (new: src/enrichment/config_change_tracker.rs)
Watch for config file changes at the filesystem level and correlate with recent sessions:
- After each scrape, scan for recently modified config files (mtime within last 24h)
- For each modified config file, find sessions that ended within 2h before the modification
- Record the correlation as an annotation: config_file_changed_after_session
- Store in: ~/.agentscribe/config-changes/<date>.json

## New: agentscribe config-changes command
agentscribe config-changes --since 7d
  Lists: config file, modification time, correlated session IDs, session outcomes

agentscribe config-changes --file CLAUDE.md
  History of all detected CLAUDE.md changes with correlated sessions

## MCP tool addition
New MCP tool: agentscribe_config_changes
  params: {since_days: int, file_pattern: string}
  returns: list of {config_file, modified_at, correlated_sessions: [{session_id, outcome, summary}]}

## Acceptance Criteria
- Config file changes detected and correlated with sessions
- agentscribe config-changes command works
- MCP tool exposed
- Patterns list configurable in config.toml: [reflection] config_file_patterns = [...]

- An invalid routing value (e.g. type_routing = {x = "bogus"}) is rejected at validation, not at parse time.
- Unknown runtime type values route to 'skip' with a warning, never panic.
- Existing plugins without [source.envelope] validate and behave unchanged.
